purpose: Journal of Food Science v4' section 3.3: head-to-head comparison of chemical-data preprocessing pipelines on the same 250 beers, same 50 sensory targets, same frozen 5-fold outer split, same model families and hyperparameters.
reporting_rule: ALL registered arms x models x folds are reported. No model, target, fold, or metric may be dropped after seeing results. No post-hoc swapping of primary metric. If only a subset of model families improves, the conclusion MUST be written as family-dependent effect, not as overall superiority.

data.X: analysis_2026a/official/附件/1.csv (250 x 231 numeric features, beer-indexed)
data.y: analysis_2026a/official/附件/4.csv (250 x 50 continuous sensory targets)
data.split: analysis_2026a/q1/splits/outer.csv (5 equal folds, seed 2601731, no label access)
data.note: 8.xlsx Calibrated chemical dataset is NOT used as model input in this experiment; input-source comparison is a separate question.

A_plain.label: Routine preprocessing (baseline)
A_plain.interpretation: Plain z-score on the raw numeric table, no chemical-unit priors, no winsorisation.

B_log.label: Arm JIA (q1 log pipeline)
B_log.interpretation: signed_log on ~verified_log columns (194), fold-wise 1/99% winsorisation, median/IQR scaling.

B_increment.label: Arm YI (q1_v2 IncrementTransform pipeline)
B_increment.interpretation: signed_log only on 33 verified-identity columns, by_source scaling (mean/std for verified-log columns, median/IQR elsewhere), explicit sentinel -1.81781854 indicator columns.

arms_note: All three arms use the SAME IncrementTransform class (a subclass of FoldTransform). A_plain output is asserted bit-identical to legacy FoldTransform(plain) output. JIA and YI both carry clip=0.01, so their mutual contrast isolates shape/scale/special only.
model_note: All hyperparameters are fixed and NOT tuned per arm, so no arm receives an optimisation advantage. Any data-dependent quantity (KRR median-distance bandwidth, target mean/sd) is computed on the training fold only.

ladder.note: L0=A_plain, L3=B_log, L6=B_increment. Isolates the marginal contribution of each preprocessing switch.

primary_metric: macro RMSE over 50 targets on pooled 250 out-of-fold predictions, in the original 4.csv continuous scale
secondary_metrics: per-target Spearman rho between OOF prediction and truth
inference: Per target: paired Wilcoxon signed-rank on the 250 per-sample squared-error differences (A minus B); positive means B is better.
Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction across the 50 targets within each (arm, model) contrast.
Cross-model consistency: number of registered models whose macro RMSE improves, reported in full, never subset-selected.
excluded_by_rule: R2 / nRMSE / error-reduction percent as primary evidence (same information as RMSE scaled by target sd)
any head-to-head claim against Nature Communications numbers
selective reporting of only winning models
